topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations regarding the complexity and importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core operational logic, nomenclature rules, and central biochemical role of C3 that define the complement system.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that detect targets and assemble convertases to reach the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary immunological actions triggered downstream of complement activation to clear and destroy pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that prevent self-damage by controlling and inactivating complement on host cell surfaces.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies in individual complement components produce distinct clinical pathologies and disease susceptibilities.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the mechanisms pathogens employ to resist complement-mediated destruction and how these bacterial factors are applied in medicine and research.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
